title: WITNESS://BACKTRACE - 2084 evidence registry
scope_note: This registry traces published public claims. It cannot verify the 2084 Sovereign Engine, a neural lifetime prison, or a universal civic ledger. Source links and the associated real-world claims require periodic human re-review.

entries.supported_claim: FTC reports and consent actions document substantial data collection and sensitive location-data sales.
entries.limitation: Zero-party data is volunteered; the evidence does not demonstrate universal monitoring of every action.

entries.supported_claim: CFPB explains existing algorithmic decision practices and applicable obligations.
entries.limitation: Not every model is a deep neural network, and an algorithm is not exempt from applicable adverse-action explanation rules.

entries.supported_claim: Regulators recognize disability risks in algorithmic hiring; EU law prohibits specified emotion-recognition practices.
entries.limitation: This does not establish that all employers deploy valid micro-expression detectors.

entries.supported_claim: Documented communication-compliance tools can screen selected organizational messages.
entries.limitation: Product capabilities do not establish universal automated punishment for employee dissent.

entries.supported_claim: Delegated authorization protocols and centralized identity dependencies are real.
entries.limitation: OAuth 2.0 alone does not mandate behavioral surveillance or deny essential services.

entries.supported_claim: Research and accommodations guidance support concerns about false flags and access barriers.
entries.limitation: A gaze alert is not proof of cheating; not all grading systems penalize neurodivergence.

entries.supported_claim: Third-party employment dossiers and algorithmic scoring can fall under consumer-reporting law.
entries.limitation: No evidence of instantaneous legal access to every health, social, and payment record.

entries.supported_claim: FTC's specific Deere proceeding concerns software and repair access.
entries.limitation: This is not proof that all vendors arbitrarily remotely disable purchased devices.

entries.supported_claim: NIST documented error-rate variation and FTC filed a facial-recognition enforcement case.
entries.limitation: No unified public-private civic-ranking index has been demonstrated by these sources.

entries.mechanism: Graph models for connected financial risk
entries.supported_claim: Graph-based transaction analysis is demonstrated in published financial fraud research.
entries.limitation: Research does not prove political guilt-by-association or universal friend-based credit punishment.
